chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, all from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a believing servant commits a sin, Allah grants him a respite of seven hours. If he seeks forgiveness from Allah, no record is kept against him; but if the hours pass and he does not seek forgiveness, one evil deed is recorded against him. Indeed, the believer is reminded of his sin even after twenty years, so he seeks forgiveness from his Lord and He forgives him; whereas the unbeliever forgets it from the moment he commits it.
ai.seo_question: How long does Allah give a believer to repent before a sin is recorded?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'tadhiir' (delayed recording) in Shia theology, illustrating the balance between divine justice and mercy by granting believers a grace period to repent. It contrasts the believer's persistent self-awareness of sin, which motivates continuous repentance even after decades, with the disbeliever's spiritual heedlessness. This mechanism underscores the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of immediate tawbah and the enduring nature of God's forgiveness for those who remain conscious of their faults.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Abu Ali Al Ashary and Muhammad Bin Yahya, altogether from Al Husayn Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Fazal Bin Ayoub, from Abdul Samad Bin Bashir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Momin servant, when he commits a sin, Allahazwj would Respite him for seven hours. So if he were to seek Forgiveness of Allahazwj, nothing would be Written against him; and if the seven hours pass by and he does not seek Forgiveness, one evil deed would be Written against him; and if the Momin remembers his sin after twenty year and he seeks Forgiveness of his Lordazwj, so Heazwj would Forgive him; but the Kafir (unbeliever) would forget it from its time’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Abu Ali al-Ash’ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya all from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When a believing servant (of Allah) commits a sin Allah gives him seven hours respite. If he pleads for forgiveness from Allah within such time nothing will be written against him. If the hours pass and he did not plead for forgiveness one sin will be written against him. A believer remembers his sin even after twenty years so that he may plead to his Lord for forgiveness and He forgives him. An unbeliever forgets his sin within the same hour.”’
